draft.title: Managing coasts
card: Waves and currents wear away coasts and move sand along them. This is coastal erosion. People manage coasts to protect land, homes and beaches from it.
building solid structures. A sea wall is a barrier along the shore that blocks waves. A groyne is a wall built out into the sea to trap sand moving along the beach.
working with natural processes. Beach nourishment adds sand to a beach. Replanting dunes uses plant roots to hold sand in place.
Hard structures can protect one place but move erosion elsewhere. A groyne traps sand, so the beach further along the coast may get less sand and wear away faster.
draft.remember: Hard engineering builds structures and can shift erosion elsewhere. Soft approaches work with natural processes.

a.q: Which of these is a soft approach to managing a coast?
opts: Building a sea wall along the shore
Building groynes out into the sea
Placing a solid barrier at the base of a cliff
a.why: Replanting dunes works with natural processes, because roots hold the sand in place. Sea walls and groynes are solid structures, so they are hard engineering.
a.clue: Which one uses plants or sand instead of building a structure?

b.q: A council builds a groyne to hold sand on Wavecrest Beach. Soon after, the next beach along the coast starts to lose sand faster. What is the most likely reason?
opts: The groyne trapped sand that would have reached it
The groyne added extra sand to that beach
The groyne stopped waves from reaching the coast
The groyne helped dune plants grow on that beach
b.why: A groyne traps sand moving along the shore, so less sand reaches the next beach and it erodes faster. The groyne does not add sand. It also does not stop all waves from reaching the coast.
b.clue: Think about where the sand moving along the beach ends up.

wants.brief: A simple side-on and top-down diagram of a beach showing a sea wall along the shore and a groyne built out into the sea, with sand building up on one side of the groyne. Labels: sea wall, groyne, sand, waves, direction sand moves.
wants.why: It shows students how each hard structure sits on the coast and how a groyne traps sand.

b.best: The groyne trapped sand that would have reached it
